name: Neo-nationalism
summary: Neo-nationalism is the nationalist and nativist current of the 2010s in the West that defends national sovereignty, borders, identity and culture against supranational bodies, globalisation and mass immigration. It holds that every nation has the right to govern itself and put its own interests first, rejects global governance, and casts the domestic elite as detached from or betraying the nation. Its leaders mostly define belonging by culture and history, though a strand also speaks of race.
scope: The national question as stated by the 2010s Western and Central European nativist-nationalist current, drawn from Trump's inaugural and UN speeches, Orban's 2014 and 2022 Tusnadfurdo speeches and Bergmann's scholarly account. A party's or government's wider economic, welfare and social programme is left out unless the nationalist texts state it as part of the national cause; classical ethnic nationalism and national variants in Asia and the Middle East are outside it.

sources.author: Office of the Hungarian Prime Minister
sources.usedFor: Migration, mixed-race versus mixed-peoples, nations that mix are no longer nations, leaving each nation to decide whom it lives alongside.

sources.title: Understanding Nativist Populism (chapter 2 of Neo-Nationalism: The Rise of Nativist Populism)
sources.author: Eirikur Bergmann, Palgrave Macmillan 2020 (open-access copy on PubMed Central)
sources.usedFor: Scholarly account of the shared qualities of neo-nationalists: nativism, cultural rather than biological exclusion, Euroscepticism, protectionism, anti-elitism.

nation-first.rationale: Trump's inaugural makes 'America First' the rule for every decision and says it is every nation's right to put its own interests first; his UN speech says wise leaders put their own people and country first, and Orban rebuilds the state on national interests.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Bergmann lists stemming immigration among the shared qualities of neo-nationalists, and both Trump and Orban speak of bringing back or defending borders against migration; the legal level is mostly discussed through illegal and non-European inflows.

open-borders.rationale: Trump calls open-border activists' policies cruel and evil and says every nation has the absolute right to protect its borders; Orban defends border closure and says the post-Western countries have lost their nationhood by mixing.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Trump chooses independence and cooperation over global governance, says the ICC has no authority, and refuses the UN migration compact; Bergmann records suspicion of multilateral institutions as a shared quality.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Trump says sovereignty must be protected above all and that the future belongs to sovereign nations; Bergmann says neo-nationalists are most often staunchly Eurosceptic, though Orban stays in the EU and fights it over national interest.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Trump says the US will never surrender its sovereignty to unelected global bodies, refuses the ICC's jurisdiction and says migration should not be governed by an international body; Bergmann reports suspicion of international bodies as typical.

national-self-determination.rationale: Trump says sovereign and independent nations are the only vehicle in which freedom, democracy and peace have survived and honours each nation's right to its own customs; Orban asks that each nation decide whom it lives alongside.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Trump says every nation has a history, culture and heritage worth defending, that the free world must embrace its national foundations, and Orban's state is rebuilt around the nation's community and culture.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Orban says Hungarians do not want to become a mixed race and that countries mixing European and non-European peoples are no longer nations, while Trump rejects prejudice by colour and Bergmann finds neo-nationalists define belonging by culture and let integrated immigrants' descendants in; strands differ.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Trump's inaugural says a small group in the capital reaped the rewards while the people bore the cost and the establishment protected itself, and Bergmann names anti-elitism and the claim that elites betray the people as core to neo-nationalism.

national-mission.rationale: Trump says the US does not seek to impose its way of life on anyone and Orban asks only to be left alone and says he does not want to tell others how to live.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trump says protection will lead to great prosperity and protects borders against other countries' goods, and Bergmann reports that neo-nationalists are more usually protectionist of national production.

free-trade.rationale: Trump blames decades of open trade for the loss of American industry and demands fair and reciprocal trade, and Bergmann reports protectionism as usual among neo-nationalists, though some claim to be economic liberals.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Trump's UN speech says the US strengthened laws to screen foreign investment for national security threats and urges others to do so, and Orban's government bought back a bank to protect community assets from foreign hands.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Trump says the ICC has no jurisdiction, legitimacy or authority over any country's citizens, and Bergmann reports suspicion of international institutions as a shared quality of neo-nationalists.

national-rebirth.rationale: Trump's inaugural promises to stop American carnage and make America great again under a new vision, and Bergmann describes neo-nationalists as restoring a golden age after crisis; the statement's word 'radical' is not stated.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Trump's inaugural ties total allegiance to the nation to jobs for American workers and says a nation exists to serve its citizens, and Bergmann says neo-nationalists voice those who lost out to globalisation.

restore-past-order.rationale: Bergmann describes neo-nationalists as nostalgic and resisting social change, while Trump's inaugural says it is looking only to the future; the sources split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Trump says each nation's culture is special and to be honoured without ranking them, while Bergmann notes that neo-nationalists' claims of European superiority rest implicitly on culture; the sources split.
